title: Identifying the Zone-Forming Candle
hook: Correction #2 creates the zone, but the zone isn’t the whole correction. It’s one candle.

launchpad.outcome: Pick the zone-forming candle: the last opposite-colour candle of Correction #2 before BOS #3, for both demand and supply.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Why is the zone one candle and not the whole correction?

takeaways: Demand: the last bearish candle of Correction #2 before buyers produce BOS #3.
Supply: the last bullish candle of Correction #2 before sellers produce BOS #3.
Don’t mark the whole correction as the zone.
The working model uses that candle’s full high-to-low range for the zone boundaries. RULE REQUIRES DAYLI CONFIRMATION.
remember: ONE CANDLE. THE LAST ONE. BEFORE BOS #3.

slides.headline: The zone is one candle.
slides.line: Correction #2 creates the zone. Inside it, you’re looking for one specific candle, not the whole pullback.

steps.label: Find the opposite-colour candles in it
steps.sub: Bearish candles for demand (bullish model). Bullish candles for supply (bearish model).

steps.label: Take the LAST one before BOS #3
steps.sub: That one candle creates the zone. Not the first one, and not the whole correction.

slides.kicker: Step 2 · Watch it on a chart
slides.headline: More than one bearish candle. Take the last.
slides.line: Bullish example, on the 5M. BOS #1, Correction #1 and BOS #2 are already marked.

steps.caption: Correction #2 has more than one bearish candle. The zone comes from the last one.
The zone candle. The last bearish candle of Correction #2. Its full high-to-low range marks a potential demand zone.
BOS #3. Buyers close a 5M candle above the high Correction #2 pulled back from. Now the zone is active.

slides.kicker: Step 3 · One candle, not the correction
slides.headline: Mark the candle, not the whole pullback.
slides.line: Correction #2 creates the zone. The zone itself is one candle.

versus.label: The zone candle
points: The last opposite-colour candle of Correction #2.

versus.label: The whole correction
points: It’s where the zone comes from.
Don’t mark all of it as the zone.

check.prompt: Correction #2 has five candles. What do you mark as the zone?

options.label: All five candles of Correction #2
options.feedback: Don’t mark the whole correction as the zone. Correction #2 creates the zone, but the zone is one candle.

options.label: The last opposite-colour candle before BOS #3
options.why: Right. That one candle creates the zone.

slides.headline: Bullish model. Find the demand candle.
slides.line: Correction #2 is marked. The last candle on the chart is BOS #3.
slides.ask: Tap the last bearish candle of Correction #2 before BOS #3.
slides.why: That’s the last bearish candle of Correction #2 before buyers produce BOS #3. It creates the demand zone.

after.caption: Demand zone. The working model uses this candle’s full high-to-low range. BOS #3 activated it.

slides.headline: Bearish model. Find the supply candle.
slides.line: Correction #2 is marked. The last candle on the chart is BOS #3.
slides.ask: Tap the last bullish candle of Correction #2 before BOS #3.
slides.why: That’s the last bullish candle of Correction #2 before sellers produce BOS #3. It creates the supply zone.

after.caption: Supply zone. The working model uses this candle’s full high-to-low range. BOS #3 activated it.

slides.quote: Don’t mark the whole correction. Find the last candle.

slides.prompt: In your own words, how do you find the zone-forming candle for demand and for supply?
slides.modelAnswer: First I find Correction #2, the pullback after BOS #2. For demand, I take the last bearish candle of Correction #2 before buyers produce BOS #3. For supply, I take the last bullish candle of Correction #2 before sellers produce BOS #3. I mark that one candle, not the whole correction. The working model uses its full high-to-low range, and that detail still needs Dayli’s confirmation.
